# PulsePic

> PulsePic is a free web app for phones that makes any picture pulse to the beat of a song. Add a picture and a song; PulsePic analyzes the song on the phone to find the tempo, every beat and the start of each bar, and animates the picture with beat-synced effects. You can export a 1080p MP4 for Instagram Reels, Stories or TikTok, or create a share link to a page with the pulsing picture, the song and artist info.

Key facts:
- Website: https://pulsepic.com (open on a phone; nothing to install; works in Safari on iPhone and Chrome on Android).
- Price: free.
- Effects: Glow, Shake, Flash, Tilt, Bounce, Echo, Rings, Sparks, RGB split, Bars, Strobe, Circle. Presets: Chill, Club, Hype.
- Sync modes: Beat, Kick, All hits. Offset slider from -300 to +300 ms.
- Video export: 9:16 (1080×1920), 1:1 (1080×1080), 4:5 (1080×1350); 15, 30, 60 or 90 seconds or the full song; MP4 (H.264 + AAC); made on the phone, not uploaded.
- Share links: page with pulsing picture, song, song name, artist, album and website; jam counter (a play counts after 5 seconds, once per browser per day).
- Guest share links are deleted after 30 days; signing in with Google or Apple keeps links forever and allows editing without changing the URL.
- Audio: MP3, M4A, AAC, WAV, AIFF, FLAC, OGG. WAV/AIFF/FLAC are converted to MP3 (192 kbps stereo) on the phone before upload; 40 MB maximum after compression.

## Guides

- [How PulsePic Finds the Beat in Any Song](https://pulsepic.com/blog/how-beat-detection-works): PulsePic analyzes your whole song before it plays. It measures how the energy changes across about 40 frequency bands, works out the tempo (BPM), then lines up every beat and the first beat of each bar. Because the beats are known ahead of time, effects land exactly on the beat instead of a moment late.
- [12 Beat-Synced Effects for Your Cover Art (and 3 One-Tap Presets)](https://pulsepic.com/blog/beat-synced-effects-and-presets): PulsePic has 12 effects that fire on the beat: Glow, Shake, Flash, Tilt, Bounce, Echo, Rings, Sparks, RGB split, Bars, Strobe and Circle. Turn on as many as you like, or tap a preset: Chill (soft glow, rings and echo), Club (glow, flash, rings, bars and tilt) or Hype (almost everything at full strength).
- [How to Turn a Song and a Picture Into a Video for Instagram Reels, Stories and TikTok](https://pulsepic.com/blog/instagram-reels-stories-video): Open PulsePic on your phone, add a picture and a song, pick your effects, then tap 🎬 Video. Choose Story / Reel (9:16), Square (1:1) or Feed (4:5), pick 15, 30, 60 or 90 seconds or the full song, and tap Record video. PulsePic makes a 1080p MP4 you can save to your phone and post to Instagram, TikTok or anywhere else.
- [How to Share Your Song as a Link With a Pulsing Picture and Artist Info](https://pulsepic.com/blog/share-song-link-with-artist-info): In the PulsePic player, tap Share, confirm you own the music or have permission, and tap Create link. You get a pulsepic.com link to a page that plays your song with your pulsing picture and effects, and shows the song name, artist, album and a button to your website. Links without an account last 30 days; sign in with Google or Apple to keep them forever.
- [What "This Has Been Jammed X Times" Means: How PulsePic Counts Plays](https://pulsepic.com/blog/jam-counter-song-plays): The jam counter at the top of every PulsePic share page shows how many times the song has been played. A play counts once someone has listened for at least 5 seconds, and each browser counts at most once per day, so quick taps and replays don't inflate the number. You can see the count for each of your links in My links.
- [Can I Use a WAV File? Uploading Studio Masters to PulsePic](https://pulsepic.com/blog/upload-wav-studio-files): Yes. PulsePic works with WAV, AIFF and FLAC files as well as MP3, M4A, AAC and OGG. The beat is found from your original file. If you create a share link, PulsePic converts studio files to a high-quality MP3 on your phone first, so the upload is small and the share page loads fast. The original file never leaves your phone.
- [How to Edit a PulsePic Share Link Without Changing the URL](https://pulsepic.com/blog/edit-share-link-without-changing-url): Sign in, tap your account button, open My links and tap Edit on the song. PulsePic opens it in the player, where you can change the effects, strength, sync mode, song details and picture. Tap Save changes and the same link updates for everyone, usually within a minute. Your jam count is kept.
- [Do My Files Stay Private? How PulsePic Handles Your Picture, Song and Account](https://pulsepic.com/blog/privacy-files-and-accounts): Your picture and song stay on your phone while you use PulsePic: the beat analysis, effects and video export all happen on the device. Files are only uploaded when you tap Create link to make a share page. You don't need an account to use PulsePic; signing in with Google or Apple just keeps your share links forever instead of 30 days.

## Optional

- [Terms & Copyright](https://pulsepic.com/terms): users keep all rights; files are stored only to play their share page; never sold or reused; report/takedown via the Report link on any share page.
- [About PulsePic](https://pulsepic.com/about): built as a free replacement for weekly-subscription phone apps like BeatLeap; more features coming; the aim is to keep it free.
- [Blog index](https://pulsepic.com/blog)
